chunks: And by this chain, from Sahl, from Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān, from Hārūn ibn al-Jahm, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I heard Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: When al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī (عليه السلام) was at the point of death, he said to al-Ḥusayn: O my brother, I entrust you with a وصية, so preserve it. When I die, prepare me, then direct me toward the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) so that I may renew my عهد with him, then take me to my mother Fāṭimah (عليها السلام), then return me and bury me in al-Baqīʿ. And know that there shall come upon me from al-Ḥumayrāʾ what the people know of her conduct, her enmity toward Allah and His Messenger (صلى الله عليه وآله), and her enmity toward us, the Ahl al-Bayt.

When al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) passed away and was placed upon his bier, they proceeded with him to the place of salat of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), where he used to perform salat over the dead. Then salat was performed over al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام). After the salat over him had been performed, he was carried and brought into the masjid. When he was brought to the grave of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), the news reached ʿĀʾishah, and it was said to her: They have come with al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī to bury him with the Messenger of Allah.

So she came out hastily on a saddled mule, and she was the first woman in Islam to ride a saddle. She stopped and said: Move your son away from my house, for nothing shall be buried in it, nor shall the Messenger of Allah have his sanctity violated. Then al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, may the salawāt of Allah be upon them both, said to her: Long ago, you and your father violated the sanctity of the Messenger of Allah, and you brought into his house one whose nearness the Messenger of Allah did not love; and Allah will question you about that, O ʿĀʾishah.

My brother instructed me to bring him near to his father, the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), so that he may renew his عهد with him. And know that my brother is the most knowledgeable of people concerning Allah and His Messenger, and the most knowledgeable concerning the taʾwīl of His Book, far above violating the Messenger of Allah in his privacy, for Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says:
O you who believe, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you.
Yet you brought men into the house of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) without his permission. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:
O you who believe, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet.
By my life, you struck the pickaxes for your father and his Fārūq near the ear of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله). And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:
Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah, those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for taqwa.

By my life, your father and his Fārūq, by their nearness to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), brought harm upon him, and they did not observe of his right what Allah had commanded them through the tongue of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله): Indeed, Allah has made inviolable from the believers in death what He has made inviolable from them in life. And by Allah, O ʿĀʾishah, had this matter that you disliked—namely the burial of al-Ḥasan near his father, the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله)—been permissible between us and Allah, you would have known that he would certainly have been buried, even despite your humiliation.

He said: Then Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah spoke and said: O ʿĀʾishah, one day on a mule and another day on a camel—so you neither control yourself nor possess the earth, out of enmity toward Banī Hāshim. He said: So she turned to him and said: O son of al-Ḥanafiyyah, these are the Fāṭimahs speaking, so what place has your speech?

Then al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام) said to her: How can you exclude Muḥammad from the Fāṭimahs? By Allah, three Fāṭimahs gave birth to him: Fāṭimah bint ʿImrān ibn ʿĀʾidh ibn ʿAmr ibn Makhzūm; Fāṭimah bint Asad ibn Hāshim; and Fāṭimah bint Zāʾidah ibn al-Aṣamm ibn Rawāḥah ibn Ḥijr ibn ʿAbd Maʿīṣ ibn ʿĀmir.

He said: Then ʿĀʾishah said to al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام): Move your son away and take him, for you are a contentious people. He said: So al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام) went to the grave of his mother, then took him away and buried him in al-Baqīʿ.

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: the People of the Household of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله)
key_terms.الْبَقِيعِ: the cemetery of al-Baqīʿ in Madinah
key_terms.الْحُمَيْرَاءِ: a reference to ʿĀʾishah in this report
key_terms.تَأْوِيلِ: the deeper interpretation or true meaning of the Book
key_terms.حِجَابُهُ: his sanctity, privacy, or protected boundary
key_terms.عَهْدًا: a renewed bond, covenant, or final connection
key_terms.وَصِيَّةٍ: a final bequest or instruction entrusted before death

ai.seo_question: What happened at the funeral of Imam al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام), and how did Imam al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام) respond?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the final وصية of Imam al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام), the events surrounding his funeral, and the obstruction of his being brought near the grave of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله). It also records Imam al-Ḥusayn’s احتجاج using Qur'anic verses about the sanctity of the Prophet’s house and proper conduct in his presence. The report is significant in Shia tradition for its historical account of the suffering of the Ahl al-Bayt and their knowledge, dignity, and rights.
